claims.text: A near-equimolar TiZrNbMoV alloy can be synthesized from blended elemental powders by LENS.
SEBM is a suitable fabrication route for Group IV-V refractory HEAs such as TiZrNbMoV or WTaMoNbV.
The starting Group IV-V elemental powder blend inherently contains C, O, and N impurities and has segregation tendencies.
High-energy-density beam processing produces rapid solidification rates of 10^4–10^6 K/s.
A 24-hour vacuum anneal at 1000–1300°C is an applicable post-processing route after additive manufacturing.
SEBM can be performed with a build temperature of about 920°C and a layer thickness of 50 μm.
A vacuum below 10^-3 Pa during processing minimizes interstitial uptake.
Post-processing annealing relieves residual stresses and dissolves brittle secondary phases.
The proposed AM and heat-treatment route yields a homogeneous ultrafine-grained BCC solid solution.
The proposed route suppresses segregation and brittle B2 or Laves phases.
The proposed route reduces the concentration of interstitial impurities at grain boundaries.
Rapid solidification during AM creates a nonequilibrium microstructure with high dislocation density and fine grains.
Decreasing grain size strengthens the alloy through Hall–Petch strengthening and improves mechanical performance.
High-temperature vacuum annealing produces diffusion-driven chemical homogenization.
High-temperature vacuum annealing reduces porosity.
Vacuum annealing mitigates Jahn–Teller-related electronic instabilities responsible for brittle-to-ductile transitions in refractory alloys.
The processed alloy will have a single-phase BCC structure.
The processed alloy will have significantly better room-temperature ductility than a cast counterpart.
The processed alloy will have significantly better high-temperature creep resistance than a cast counterpart.
Evaporation of volatile Al or V during high-temperature AM can alter stoichiometry and thereby cause unexpected phases or porosity.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes 920°C preheating/melting plus the 1000–1300°C anneal as a 'two-stage vacuum heat treatment,' whereas the intervention and conditions identify 920°C as the SEBM build temperature and reserve heat treatment for the subsequent anneal.
